title: Rica tomato (Rica kamatis): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Rica tomato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Rica tomato is a tomato variety. 63 to 65 days to harvest, 13.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Rica is a registered tomato variety, also sold or known as Rica kamatis. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2005 as NSIC 2005 Tm 12. It takes 63 to 65 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 13.85 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Rica tomato takes 63 to 65 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is 6.6 days faster than the average of the 20 tomato varieties with a day count, 70.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 13.85 t/ha trails the average of its group, 20.91. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives first harvest 63 to 65 days after transplanting in registration trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 10 t/ha in the dry season and 17.5 t/ha in the wet season in registration trials.
**Season:** Trial yields were higher in the wet season.
**Where:** The registry says it suits a wide range of growing conditions.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: NSIC registered public tomato from IPB UPLB, no current DA promotion or seller found. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Rica tomato

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Rica kamatis the same as Rica?
items.a: Yes. Rica kamatis is another name for Rica, registered as NSIC 2005 Tm 12. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 63 to 65 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 13.85 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Rica?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
